answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I spent the Spark bank on the biggest attack first: Rapid Fire, which prints 2 but shows 0, for 4 damage four times into the only enemy — 16 damage, and Nibbit is the sole target so all four hits land on it. That consumed the 3 Sparks, so Kaboom! reverted to its printed cost of 1; I paid it for 7 more damage, putting Nibbit at 20 of 43. My last energy went to Imaginary Friend for 5 Block, 3 Burst Energy and Burst +5, taking the meter from 20 toward the top. Nibbit's 12 lands into 5 Block, so I take 7 and end at 35/62. Total energy spent: 0 + 1 + 1 = 2, exactly what I had.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Rapid Fire, then Duck and Cover, then Imaginary Friend — 10 Block against the telegraphed 12, taking only 2 damage instead of 7. I weighed it and dropped it: 5 extra HP is cheap at 42/62 with no second attacker on the board, and Kaboom!'s 7 damage is worth more against a 43 HP enemy I want dead a turn sooner. I also briefly checked the ordering question — making Kaboom! the free card instead of Rapid Fire — and rejected it immediately, since the discount is worth 2 energy on Rapid Fire and only 1 on Kaboom!, and spending it on the 16-damage card rather than the 7-damage one is not close.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: 5 HP, and Duck and Cover stays unplayed in hand for whatever the discard rule does with it. I also gave up nothing on the Burst side by choosing Imaginary Friend over Duck and Cover — that swap was free — so the whole cost of the line is the 5 HP I chose not to block, traded for 7 damage now.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. If Nibbit had telegraphed something big enough that 5 Block left me in real trouble — say an attack in the mid-20s or higher, or a multi-hit that ate the block cheaply — I would have cut Kaboom! for Duck and Cover and stacked 10 Block, conceding the 7 damage. A defensive or buffing intent with no incoming damage would have pushed me the other way, but there was nothing else damaging I could afford, so the same three cards would have been played with the block simply wasted. The 12 sits in the middle: survivable bare, so the block is a convenience and the damage is the point.
